idiom_name: token type with an internal constructor (module-scoped grant); file-private is narrower but cannot appear in public signatures
implementation_notes: Kotlin replaces friendship with two scopes: internal is visible everywhere in the same module (a Gradle source set, Maven project or IDEA module), and a private top-level declaration is visible in its file only. A private constructor is visible inside its own class, and the enclosing class cannot reach a nested class's private constructor - the Kotlin compiler reports 'cannot access constructor(): it is private in Key' - so the C++ and Java shapes do not port. The passkey therefore becomes a public token type whose constructor is internal: the signature stays public, the grant is the module, and the narrower alternative is rejected by the compiler itself ('public function exposes its internal parameter type') when the token type is internal. If the grant must name exactly one collaborator, Kotlin cannot express it; split the module or route the call through a type the collaborator already owns.
pitfalls: internal is module-sized - and the test source set sees main's internals by default - so tests and sibling modules can mint keys.
Kotlin refuses to expose an internal type in a public signature; keep the token type public with an internal constructor instead of making the token itself internal.
A nested class's private constructor is invisible to the enclosing class, so a key nested in the authorised class cannot be constructed there.
